title: Nebraska AI Laws

reading.body:
Nebraska has enacted one AI-related law, LB525, which pairs agricultural data privacy with safety duties for conversational AI operators, including minors.

LB525, passed on April 17, 2026, does two separate things. The Agricultural Data Privacy Act gives agricultural producers ownership and control of data from their farm, land, devices, and equipment, prohibits selling that data without express written consent, and requires reasonable data security. The Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act imposes disclosure, content prevention, privacy tool, and crisis protocol duties on operators of conversational AI services, with specific attention to minor account holders. The law also amends the public records law to allow withholding agricultural data absent prior written consent from the owner.

For AI, this law treats the technology as a data governance and consumer safety problem, not as a compute or infrastructure problem. The agricultural data provisions create a consent boundary around farm data that could otherwise be used for AI training or analytics. The conversational AI provisions place operational duties on services that interact with users, especially minors. The law does not address model training, data centers, or energy use, and it does not indicate how these duties will be enforced or whether other AI-related bills are pending in Nebraska.

Enacted AI laws in Nebraska

  • LB525: Adopt the Agricultural Data Privacy Act and the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act passed 2026-04-17

    The law adopts the Agricultural Data Privacy Act, which gives agricultural producers ownership and control of agricultural data originating from their farm, land, devices, and equipment, and prohibits controllers and processors from selling that data without express written consent while requiring reasonable data security. It also adopts the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act, which imposes disclosure, content prevention, privacy tool, and crisis protocol duties on operators of conversational artificial intelligence services, especially for minor account holders. It amends the public records law to allow withholding agricultural data absent prior written consent from the owner.
